title: How to Handle Loneliness
excerpt: Loneliness is not a character flaw and it is not always solved by being around people. It is a signal, and the question is what you do with it.
body:
The first thing to say about loneliness is that it is not a sin and it is not a weakness. Even Jesus, in the garden, asked his friends to stay near and watch with him, and grieved that they could not (Matthew 26:38-40). The God who made us said before anything had gone wrong, before sin, that it is not good for the human to be alone (Genesis 2:18). So if you are lonely, you are not malfunctioning. You are responding correctly to a real lack. The ache is doing its job. The question is what you do with the signal, because loneliness handled badly becomes a prison, and loneliness handled well becomes a door.

## Tell the difference between solitude and isolation

These are not the same thing, and confusing them keeps people stuck. Solitude is being alone and at peace, the chosen quiet where you meet God and yourself. Isolation is being alone and aching, cut off from the connection you were made for. Jesus sought solitude constantly, withdrawing to lonely places to pray (Luke 5:16). He did not seek isolation.

The trap is that isolation disguises itself as solitude. You tell yourself you are fine being alone, you are introverted, you do not need people, and meanwhile you are slowly withering. Be honest about which one you are in. If your aloneness restores you, it is solitude, keep it. If it drains and dims you, it is isolation, and it needs a different answer.

## Resist the instinct to withdraw

Loneliness has a cruel logic. It tells you to pull back further, that reaching out is too risky, that people would not want you anyway, that it is safer to stay in. Every one of those messages deepens the very thing it claims to protect you from. Loneliness, left alone, recruits you into your own imprisonment.

So the first move against it is almost always to push against the instinct. Go to the thing you do not feel like going to. Send the text you are afraid to send. Show up to the gathering when every cell in you wants to stay home. You will not feel like it; that is what loneliness does, it kills the appetite for the cure. Act against the feeling, not from it. Connection is built by the people who show up before they feel like it.

## Move toward others, not just toward being filled

There is a kind of lonely person who goes to people only to be filled, and stays empty, because they arrive as a need rather than a presence. Counterintuitively, one of the surest exits from loneliness is to stop hunting for someone to meet your need and start meeting someone else's. Serve. Notice the other lonely person in the room and go to them. Visit the widow, the shut-in, the new person nobody is talking to.

This is not a trick and it is not denial of your own need. It is the strange economy Jesus described, that you find your life by giving it away (Mark 8:35). The lonely person who pours out is met in the pouring, while the lonely person who only seeks to be filled often stays empty no matter how full the room.

## Let it drive you to God

Underneath every human loneliness is a deeper ache that no person was ever meant to fully fill. We keep asking spouses and friends and crowds to be God for us, and they cannot, and we call the resulting disappointment loneliness. Some of your loneliness is for people, and you should pursue people. Some of it is for God, and only he fits that hollow (Psalm 73:25-26).

This does not make human connection optional; God himself said it was not good to be alone, and then made us for each other. But it does mean a friend who expects another human to cure all of it will exhaust that human and stay lonely. Bring the deepest part of the ache to the only One who can hold it, and bring the human-shaped part of it to actual humans. Most of us mix these up, asking people for what only God gives and asking God for what he intends to give us through people.

## This week

Do the one thing your loneliness is telling you not to do. Reach out to a specific person, by name, this week. Then find someone lonelier than you and go toward them. The signal is real. The answer is a door, not a deeper room.
